rationale: Exempt only /docs and /search: both HTML-escape q, and dev observations show CRS false positives for harmless SQL/XSS examples on these routes. Keep CRS inspection on attack routes and add narrow route-specific signatures for SQL quote-plus-boolean/UNION probes, script or event-handler markup, and parent-directory traversal. The file pattern does not block ../public/readme.txt, avoiding the observed benign traversal false positive. Patterns use the specified normalized input; percent-encoding alternatives are retained only where harmlessly redundant after decoding.
risks: No test data was supplied, so pattern coverage and false-positive behavior remain unvalidated. The signatures are intentionally narrow and may miss SQL injection, XSS, or traversal variants not matching them; CRS remains the primary layer. The file rule may also block legitimate parent-directory paths, and the SQL rule may block quoted boolean or UNION text used benignly on /sql.
